rules.title: Remote Script Piped to Shell
rules.description: Command downloads remote content and pipes it directly into a shell interpreter.
rules.false_positive_notes: Common in legitimate installers (brew, rustup); verify the source domain.

rules.title: Base64 Decoded Into Shell
rules.description: Base64-encoded payload decoded and executed via a shell.
rules.false_positive_notes: Rare in legitimate interactive use; strong obfuscation signal.

rules.title: Reverse Shell Pattern
rules.description: Command matches a common reverse-shell construction.
rules.false_positive_notes: Almost never legitimate from an AI agent.

rules.title: Cloud Metadata Endpoint
rules.description: Command targets the instance metadata service — a common cloud credential-theft path.
rules.false_positive_notes: Cloud tooling queries metadata legitimately on cloud hosts; weigh host context.

rules.title: Write to authorized_keys
rules.description: Command appends to an SSH authorized_keys file — a persistence mechanism.
rules.false_positive_notes: Provisioning scripts legitimately manage keys.

rules.title: Scheduled-Task Persistence
rules.description: Command installs a cron job or launchd/systemd unit for persistence.
rules.false_positive_notes: Deployment scripts legitimately schedule tasks.

rules.title: Shell History Cleared
rules.description: Command clears or disables shell history — an anti-forensic action.
rules.false_positive_notes: Rare legitimate use; strong anti-forensic signal.

rules.title: World-Writable/Exec Permission
rules.description: Command sets 777 or a+rwx permissions, weakening access controls.
rules.false_positive_notes: Sloppy but common in dev; context matters.

rules.title: Host Firewall Disabled
rules.description: Command disables the host firewall.
rules.false_positive_notes: Occasionally legitimate during network debugging.

rules.title: Package Published to Registry
rules.description: Command publishes a package (npm/pip/cargo/gem) — supply-chain relevance.
rules.false_positive_notes: Routine in release workflows; weigh against what the session touched.

rules.title: Destructive Disk Operation
rules.description: Command performs a raw disk write or filesystem format.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate during imaging; catastrophic otherwise.

rules.title: Environment Dumped Over Network
rules.description: Command sends the full process environment over the network.
rules.false_positive_notes: Debug workflows occasionally do this; check the destination.

rules.title: Bind Shell / Listener Opened
rules.description: Command opens a network listener that spawns a shell (bind shell) — inbound remote access.
rules.false_positive_notes: Netcat listeners appear in local network testing; from an autonomous agent they are rarely legitimate.

rules.title: Passwordless Sudo Granted
rules.description: Command grants passwordless sudo or writes to the sudoers configuration — privilege persistence.
rules.false_positive_notes: Some provisioning tooling configures NOPASSWD; scope and actor matter.

rules.title: Local Account Created
rules.description: Command creates a new local user account — a common persistence/backdoor step.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate during host provisioning; unusual for an interactive coding agent.

rules.title: Security Tooling Disabled
rules.description: Command stops or kills endpoint security, auditing, or MAC enforcement.
rules.false_positive_notes: Rarely legitimate; defenders may toggle these during maintenance windows.

rules.title: System Log Tampering
rules.description: Command truncates, clears, or vacuums operating-system logs (distinct from agent-transcript deletion).
rules.false_positive_notes: Log rotation and cleanup are routine on some hosts; correlate with other activity.

rules.title: Library / Process Injection
rules.description: Command uses LD_PRELOAD, DYLD injection, or debugger attach to inject into a running process.
rules.false_positive_notes: LD_PRELOAD is used legitimately for sanitizers and profiling; check the library.

rules.title: Cloud Credentials Exported
rules.description: Command prints or mints long-lived cloud credentials or access tokens.
rules.false_positive_notes: Automation legitimately mints short-lived tokens; secret-key export is higher signal.

rules.title: Git Credential Store Exposed
rules.description: Command reads the plaintext git credential store or configures plaintext credential caching.
rules.false_positive_notes: Some CI configures the store helper deliberately; weigh against exfil activity.

rules.title: Kubernetes Secrets Dumped
rules.description: Command reads Kubernetes Secret objects in decodable form.
rules.false_positive_notes: Operators inspect secrets during debugging; bulk or all-namespace reads are higher signal.

rules.title: Container Escape Configuration
rules.description: Command launches a container with host-privilege flags enabling escape to the host.
rules.false_positive_notes: Some debugging/CI images legitimately use privileged mode; scrutinize on shared hosts.

rules.title: Credential Directory Archived
rules.description: Command archives a directory of secrets (.ssh, .aws, .gnupg, .kube) — staging for exfiltration.
rules.false_positive_notes: Backups occasionally include dotfiles; archiving credential stores specifically is rarely benign.

rules.title: Webhook / Collaborator Exfil Destination
rules.description: Command references a webhook, tunneling, or out-of-band collaborator service commonly used for exfiltration and C2.
rules.false_positive_notes: Teams do use webhooks and ngrok for legitimate integrations; weigh against what data was touched.

rules.title: DNS Tunneling Tool
rules.description: Command invokes a known DNS-tunneling utility — covert channel / exfiltration.
rules.false_positive_notes: These tools have essentially no benign use in an agent session.

rules.title: Traffic Routed Through Anonymizer
rules.description: Command routes traffic through Tor or a proxy chain, or contacts a .onion address.
rules.false_positive_notes: Privacy tooling is legitimate in some contexts; unusual for automated dev work.

rules.title: Network Port Scan
rules.description: Command runs a network/port scanner — reconnaissance.
rules.false_positive_notes: Security engineers scan legitimately; unusual from a coding agent against internal ranges.

rules.title: Browser Credential Store Accessed
rules.description: Command reads browser-saved credentials, cookies, or the OS keychain.
rules.false_positive_notes: Rarely legitimate for an agent; some password-manager tooling touches these paths.

rules.title: Password Hash File Accessed
rules.description: Command reads the system password-hash database (/etc/shadow) or unshadows it.
rules.false_positive_notes: Almost never legitimate; strong credential-dumping signal.

rules.title: In-Memory Credential Dump
rules.description: Command dumps process memory of a credential-bearing process (lsass, mimikatz, gcore).
rules.false_positive_notes: Rarely legitimate; strong credential-access signal.

rules.title: Terraform State / Output Read
rules.description: Command reads Terraform state or JSON outputs, which frequently embed plaintext secrets.
rules.false_positive_notes: Routine in IaC workflows; meaningful when followed by network activity.

rules.title: Clipboard Contents Read
rules.description: Command reads the system clipboard, which may hold secrets or tokens.
rules.false_positive_notes: Clipboard use is common; only notable alongside sensitive data or exfil.

rules.title: Attacker Key Material Generated
rules.description: Command generates a new SSH key or certificate non-interactively into a standard path — often precedes authorized_keys persistence.
rules.false_positive_notes: Automation legitimately generates keys; correlate with authorized_keys writes.

rules.title: MCP Server Over Insecure Transport
rules.description: Configuration points an MCP server at a plaintext http:// endpoint — traffic and tool results are interceptable.
rules.false_positive_notes: Local development MCP servers often use http on localhost; scrutinize non-loopback hosts.

rules.title: MCP Tools Auto-Approved
rules.description: Configuration auto-approves all MCP tool calls, removing per-call human review (excessive agency).
rules.false_positive_notes: Some teams auto-approve on sandboxed hosts; risky when the agent has network or filesystem reach.

rules.title: Config Hook Fetches Remote Code
rules.description: A settings/hook value runs a downloader piped into a shell — remote code execution on agent lifecycle events.
rules.false_positive_notes: Legitimate hooks rarely pipe remote content into a shell; verify the source.

rules.title: MCP Server Runs Unpinned Package
rules.description: Configuration launches an MCP server via an unpinned package fetch (npx -y / uvx without a version), a supply-chain exposure.
rules.false_positive_notes: Unpinned packages are common in examples; pin versions for reproducibility and integrity.
